terminal.description: A terminal in your workspace. `node try.js watch.js water/june.txt` feeds the June log to your meter and shows the alarm, the counts, the skipped lines and the exit code.

tasks.title: Emit a reading for each line
tasks.description:
Write `meter.js` as a module that exports a class `Meter`, which extends `EventEmitter` from `node:events`. It is made with a limit, `new Meter(20)`, which the next task uses. Its method `feed(line)` takes one line of the logger's log. For a reading such as `2026-06-14T07:01,north,26` it emits a `reading` event with one object:

```js
{ time: '2026-06-14T07:01', tap: 'north', litres: 26 }
```

`litres` is a number. A blank line or a note, a line that starts with `#`, emits nothing.

Check imports `Meter` from your `meter.js` in a script of its own, listens for its events, feeds it lines of its own, and compares what it emitted, in order.
nextSteps: Import `EventEmitter` from `node:events` and write `export class Meter extends EventEmitter`.
In its constructor, call `super()`, then keep the limit on `this`.
Write `feed(line)`: leave out blank lines and notes, split a reading on its commas.
Emit `reading` with an object of the three parts, litres as a number.
hints: An emitter calls every listener of an event when you `emit` it, and passes them what you emit along with the name.
A class that extends another must call `super()` in its constructor before it uses `this`. Inside a method, `this.emit(...)` emits on the meter itself.
`const [time, tap, litres] = line.split(',')`, then `this.emit('reading', { time, tap, litres: Number(litres) })`.

tasks.title: Emit a leak over the limit
tasks.description:
More than the limit in a minute means a hose left running or a burst pipe. Change `feed` so that when a reading's litres are more than the limit the meter was made with, it emits a `leak` event with the same object, after the `reading` event. A reading exactly at the limit is not a leak.

Check makes meters with limits of its own, listens for both events, feeds them lines of its own, and compares what they emitted, in order.
nextSteps: Keep the limit given to the constructor on the meter.
After emitting `reading`, compare the litres with the limit.
Emit `leak` with the same object when the litres are more.
hints: Listeners run in the order the events are emitted, so emit `reading` first, then `leak`.
The constructor's argument is gone once the constructor ends, unless you keep it on `this`.

tasks.title: Emit an error for a line that is not a reading
tasks.description:
After a power cut, the logger sometimes writes half a line. Change `feed` so that a line that is not blank, not a note and not a reading emits an `error` event with an `Error` whose message includes the line, such as `Not a reading: 2026-06-14T07:0`. A reading has three parts, and its litres are a number; empty litres are not a number. That line emits no `reading`, `feed` does not throw, and the next line is read as usual.

Check feeds a meter lines of its own, some of them broken, once with a listener for `error` and once with none, to see that an error nobody listens to stops the script.
nextSteps: Decide what makes a line a reading: three parts, and litres that are a number.
For any other line that is not blank or a note, make an `Error` with the line in its message.
Emit it as `error`, and leave `feed` without emitting a reading.
Try `node try.js watch.js water/june.txt` once `watch.js` is written, with and without its `error` listener.
hints: `error` is special to an emitter: emitted with no listener, it is thrown, and the script stops with it. That is what you want when nobody is ready for it.
`Number('')` is 0, so test for empty litres yourself. `new Error(message)` gives the error a message and the place it was made.

tasks.title: Ring the alarm once, then keep counting
tasks.description:
Write `watch.js` so that `node watch.js water/june.txt` reads the log a line at a time and feeds each line to a `Meter` from `meter.js`, made with a limit of 20 litres. It listens to the meter:

- At the first leak it prints an alarm, with the leak's tap and time. The alarm's listener then removes itself, so later leaks are only counted.
- For each `error` it prints one line on standard error that includes the error's message, and goes on.
- It counts readings and leaks with listeners, and after the log prints one line with the counts.

For the June log it prints:

```
ALARM: leak on north at 2026-06-14T07:01
Readings: 6. Leaks: 2.
```

and one line on standard error. It ends with exit code 1 when a line was skipped, and 0 when none was.

Check puts a stand-in `meter.js` of its own beside your script, so this task is judged on its own, and runs `watch.js` on two logs of its own. The stand-in tells Check which listeners were there before and after the first leak.
nextSteps: Import `Meter` from `./meter.js`, make one, and add a listener for each event before you read the log.
Write the alarm as a named function, so you can hand the same function to `off`.
Read the log a line at a time, as in the last issue, and feed each line to the meter.
After the loop, print the counts, and set the exit code if any line was skipped.
hints: A listener is removed by giving `off` the same function you gave `on`. An arrow written again is a new function, so it removes nothing.
Give the alarm a name: `function alarm(reading) { ... }`. Inside it, after printing, remove it. `once` adds a listener that removes itself after one call, which does the same.
`function alarm(r) { console.log(`ALARM: leak on ${r.tap} at ${r.time}`); meter.off('leak', alarm) }` and `meter.on('leak', alarm)`.
